cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Everything Has Two Prices
cards.instruction: Price every offer twice: once in practical terms and again through an emotional cost that grows when the offer returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lend you the dress for ten pounds and an apology for calling it hideous.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's twenty. Can I just take it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the extra ten. I'll help with the zip once you tell me what changed your mind.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, it's beautiful. Can I wear it to the party now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For ten, yes. And when they ask, tell them I chose it; don't say you rescued it from my wardrobe.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 loan has cash and apology prices; A3 returns excess money and offers zip help; A5 uses renewed party request to add public credit for taste.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 tries overpayment, A3 refuses its emotional substitution; B4 minimal praise asks loan again, causing A5 public attribution price.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 want use of the dress without the personal exposure A seeks, a credible conflict.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands private retraction into publicly crediting A judgement when the offer returns for the party.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 wardrobe-rescue prohibition is specific feared framing after hideous, not a generic lesson about respect.
